2016_091_031516mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of March 15, 2016 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Its central action is the 2015/16 budget amendment, appropriating $141,504,374 in the General Fund, $3,690,488 for Food Service, $1,950,829 for the Troy Career Center, $2,894,044 for Adult Education and Community Service, and $300,000 for Capital Maintenance. The packet also closes Bemis and Schroeder Elementary Schools to open enrollment, sets Schools of Choice at 100 kindergarten and 30 first-grade seats plus 15 at Baker Middle School, and awards $2,673,656.00 of bond site work at five buildings. The January 2016 Treasurer's Report it carries records $12,112,047.80 in total disbursements.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, March 15, 2016, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW), and at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition**
TSD Mission Moment for Boulan Park Middle School "Effective Teens" — 7th and 8th graders who practice the 7 Habits of Highly Effective Teens, mentor weekly at Bemis Elementary and pursue Genius Hour projects; teachers Mary Typinski and Michelle Slaviero. Gayle Moran of Sodexo presents checks to two high schools for the Healthy High School Challenge; no amounts are stated.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the February 2 special meeting and closed session, the February 2 workshop and the February 16 regular meeting, plus the January 2016 Treasurer's Report. Resolution 16-016 had taken the Board into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c) for mid-year superintendent evaluation and negotiations, 7 yes. The February 16 minutes record Resolution 16-017 naming February Principal Appreciation Month, roofing bid #9817 to J. D. Chandler at $1,078,282.00 and Royal West at $773,800.00 (total $1,852,082.00), and lawn mowing bid #9818 to Green Meadows Lawnscape at $112,644 per year for three years. Enrollment projections from Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants showed the District with 98 more students than projected.

January YTD reports show General Fund revenue of $63,717,316 against a $139,930,708 approved budget and expenditures of $68,032,298 against $141,360,708, with fund balance moving from 20,701,637 on January 1 to $19,271,637 on January 31. The largest register items are an MPSERS wire of 1,632,749.54 and MESSA premiums of 1,041,811.63 and 1,030,113.06.

**Personnel**
Probationary 2015-2016 contract for Lindsey Nader, 1.0 Resource Room Teacher at Hill Elementary — M.A. Oakland University 2012 (Special Education), previously a long-term substitute at Martell, Troy Union and Leonard.

**Enrollment and Schools of Choice**
Bemis and Schroeder Elementary Schools close to open enrollment for 2016/2017. Athens and Troy High remain closed except for not more than 25 incoming ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area who wish to attend Athens, applications March 21 – April 1, 2016. A memorandum from Kris Griffor and Mark Dziatczak recommends 100 kindergarten and 30 first-grade Schools of Choice seats and 15 total 6th–8th grade seats at Baker Middle School, adopted as four resolutions under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996. Elementary Schools of Choice enrollment stands at 534 against 4,996 non-SOC students, 9.7%.

**Budget amendment**

| Fund | Appropriation |

| Food Service Fund (Amendment 1) | $3,690,488 |
| Troy Career Center Fund (Amendment 1) | $1,950,829 |

| Capital Maintenance Fund (Amendment 2) | $300,000 |

General Fund revenues are amended to $140,176,947 and the ending fund balance to $19,374,210, or 13.69%.

**Construction bids** (2014 Capital Projects Fund)
Flooring at International Academy-East to Shock Brothers, $47,800.00. Site work at Troy High, Athens, Smith, Barnard and Schroeder — Metro Electric electrical $532,800.00, Cortis Brothers site work $1,973,600.00, contingency $167,256.00, total $2,673,656.00.
2016_091_031516mtg.verbose:
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting packet for March 15, 2016, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

RECOGNITION. The TSD Mission Moment honored Boulan Park Middle School's "Effective Teens" program, in which 7th and 8th grade students practice the 7 Habits of Highly Effective Teens, volunteer weekly at Bemis Elementary and complete Genius Hour projects; teachers Mary Typinski and Michelle Slaviero were recognized along with twelve students. Gayle Moran, Director of Food Services for Sodexo, presented checks to two high schools for the national Healthy High School Challenge; no dollar amounts were stated.

CONSENT AGENDA AND PRIOR MINUTES. The consent agenda carried the February 2, 2016 special meeting and closed session minutes, the February 2 workshop minutes, the February 16 regular meeting minutes and the January 2016 Treasurer's Report. The February 2 special meeting opened at 5:00 p.m. under President Philippart with members Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood and Superintendent Machesky present; Resolution 16-016, moved by Mrs. Fleming and supported by Mr. Schmidt, entered closed session "as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8 (c)" for mid-year superintendent evaluation and negotiations, carrying seven yes votes and running 5:05 p.m. to 6:47 p.m. The February 2 workshop ran 6:53 p.m. to 9:43 p.m. and covered Lusk & Albertson policies, food service strategic planning and enrollment projections. Paula Fleming, Secretary, submitted the minutes.

FEBRUARY 16 MEETING. Called to order at 7:00 p.m. before approximately 200 people, with Deputy Superintendent Mark Dziatczak seated with the Board in Superintendent Machesky's absence. Senior Scholar Athletes holding a 3.5 cumulative grade point average were recognized, along with eight All-State athletes. Resolution 16-017 recognized February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy, 7-0; Resolution 16-018 approved the consent agenda including the December 2015 Treasurer's Report and rescission of the written agreement with Weiming Education Group, 7-0. Item 8.D, Policy Services Provider — Lusk Albertson, was removed. Enrollment projections by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants showed the District with 98 more students this year than projected, and the Facilities Study Team met weekly in four groups covering attendance areas, schools of choice numbers, early childhood programs and building capacity. Resolution 16-019 awarded roofing bid #9817 to J. D. Chandler at $1,078,282.00 and Royal West at $773,800.00, total $1,852,082.00, from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and Operational Fund; Resolution 16-020 awarded lawn mowing and leaf removal bid #9818 to Green Meadows Lawnscape at $112,644 per year for three years; Resolution 16-021 awarded bid #9819 for MEP upgrades and classroom construction at IA-East and Hamilton Elementary among Professional Thermal, Titan Industries, Hewitt Company, Steel Equipment Co., Farnell Contracting, Contrast Mechanical and Great Lakes Power. Adjournment 8:12 p.m.

Consolidated Debt Service Funds (306, 307, 312, 314) show property taxes of 16,649,731 against 13,214,181, redemption of principal 11,660,000 with nothing yet drawn, interest on debt 4,922,738 against 2,541,194 and a fund balance of $970,056. Consolidated Capital Projects Funds (499, 414) show total revenue of $67,664,416 against $118,791 and a fund balance falling from 31,821,146 to $669,273.

The P-Card report for 12/28/2015 through 1/27/2016 shows a subtotal of 106,834.13, credits of (3,499.49) and total expenses of 103,334.64. The Pentamation report ACCTPA21, run 03/07/2016 for transact.yr='16' and transact.period='7', accounting period 9/16, ends in a TOTAL REPORT of 10,066,506.13, with fund totals including 1,037,355.94 for the 2014 Capital Projects Series 1 fund (414), 18,720.00 for Capital Projects Maintenance (499) and 152,579.08 for Student Activity (700). Largest items: an MPSERS wire of 1,632,749.54, MESSA premiums of 1,041,811.63 and 1,030,113.06, further MPSERS wires of 933,331.38, 923,285.10 and 735,070.20, Thermal Netics 335,500.00 for 2013 bond work at Troy High, Barton Malow 303,966.70 including a 45,203.88 construction-management fee, Enviro Clean Services 244,496.74, Sodexo Management 236,079.23, Blue Cross Blue Shield 149,263.74, Professional Ed Services 139,781.39, First Group America 133,646.65 in the General Fund and 103,409.99 in Special Education, and Oakland Schools 37,698.00 for fall 2015 VLAC students. Fund 499 paid Applied Science & Technology 13,000.00 for wetland delineation and Nowak & Fraus 5,720.00 for land surveying.

PERSONNEL (item 6.A). A probationary contract for the 2015-2016 school year for Lindsey Nader, 1.0 Resource Room Teacher at Hill Elementary. Her biographical sketch dated March 10, 2016 lists an M.A. from Oakland University, Auburn Hills, June 2012 in Special Education and a B.A. from Oakland University, June 2009 in Language Arts, with long-term substitute assignments at Martell Elementary (November 2014–June 2015), Troy Union Elementary (June 2013) and Leonard Elementary (February 2013–May 2013), and residence in Shelby Township.

CURRICULUM (items 7.A–7.F). Citing total student enrollment and physical space constraints, Bemis and Schroeder Elementary Schools are closed to open enrollment for 2016/2017. Athens and Troy High are also closed, excepting not more than 25 incoming ninth-grade students who reside in the Troy High attendance area but wish to attend Athens; applications are accepted March 21 – April 1, 2016, and students with siblings currently in grades 9–11 may open enroll to remain. A March 15, 2016 memorandum from Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, and Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent, Teaching and Learning, to Dr. Richard Machesky recommends using Fred Ignatovich's 1.5 enrollment projection numbers, accepting applications for 100 kindergarten and 30 first grade students, limiting kindergarten applicants to the full-day program, and accepting 15 total 6th, 7th and 8th grade applications for Baker Middle School, where the estimate for enrollment next year approximates to 727 (the companion presentation states 728). Supporting data show 534 Schools of Choice elementary students against 4,996 non-SOC, 9.7% overall, ranging from Schroeder at 1.7% to Hill at 18.8%; ELL 93 SOC students at 17.4% against 1372 non-SOC at 27.5%; free/reduced lunch 72 at 13.5% against 516 at 10.3%; special education 19 at 3.6% against 467 at 9.3%. The application history from 2006-2007 shows 760 kindergarten and 275 first-grade openings advertised and retention rates of 92.42% and 88.84%. Elementary enrollment for 2015-2016 totaled 5529 students against 216.5 teacher FTE, with 11,219 non-Schools of Choice students district-wide and an anticipated 67 sibling-preference students. Items 7.C through 7.F adopt the annual resolutions under Section 105 and Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996.

BUSINESS (items 8.A–8.C). The 2015-16 budget amendment covers General Fund Amendment 2, Food Service Fund Amendment 1, Troy Career Center Amendment 1, Adult Education and Community Service Fund Amendment 2 and Capital Maintenance Fund Amendment 2, appropriating $141,504,374, $3,690,488, $1,950,829, $2,894,044 and $300,000 respectively. In the General Fund, local revenue is amended from 36,040,808 to 35,908,445 and state from 93,055,841 to 93,433,779, moving total revenues from 139,930,708 to 140,176,947. Expenditures move from 141,360,708 to 141,504,374, with basic programs falling from 79,186,801 to 78,727,312, added needs rising from 15,487,781 to 16,159,653, special education rising to 10,595,055 and athletics and other support falling from 1,876,403 to 1,443,973; the budgeted deficit narrows from (1,430,000) to (1,327,427). Beginning fund balance July 1, 2015 was $20,701,637 and the budgeted ending fund balance June 30, 2016 is $19,374,210, or 13.69% against 15.08% in 2014-15 actual. Food Service ending fund balance is amended to $1,112,156, Adult Education and Community Service to $2,464,839, Capital Maintenance to $429,355, and Troy Career Center remains at $0. Item 8.B awards the reissued flooring RFP for the International Academy-East classroom construction project to Shock Brothers at $47,800.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, reviewed by Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, Christa Amalio of Barton Malow and owners representative Michelle Kerns. Item 8.C awards Bid Package 17 site work — parking lot replacement and site lighting at Troy High, Athens, Smith and Schroeder plus floodplain work at Barnard — to Metro Electric for electrical at $532,800.00 and Cortis Brothers for site work at $1,973,600.00, with a $167,256.00 contingency and a total of $2,673,656.00. Rob Carson's March 9, 2016 memorandum to Rick West notes RFP Bid 9819 issued February 5, 2016, review by TMP Associates, Peter Basso & Associates and Barton Malow, and the work commencing June 20, 2016 for August 2016 completion. Competing bid tally totals were 614,000.00 for Shoreview and 2,132,395.00 for Nagle.
